summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

David Zilberman (1938–1977) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under Yuri Levada from 1968 to 1972. He held posts at Odesa University, Hunter College, the University of Chicago, and Brandeis University.

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh (1914–1989) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Walther Wüst and held posts at the University of Munich, Alexandria University, and Uppsala University.
Daw Ohn (1913–2003) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and linguistics. She studied at the University of Rangoon, where she was attested as a Tutor in Pali in 1977.

Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) specialized in Tibetology and history. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley, and served as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University from circa 1983 to 2004.
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has held a post at Tibet University.
Dawei Wang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sichuan University and held a post there at the Institute for Daoism and Religious Culture Studies.

Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (circa 1961–1984) and chaired the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University of the Punjab under John Marshall. He held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India and served as Director of Archaeology for Jaipur State.

Dayananda Saraswati (1824–1883) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and with teachers including Virajanand Dandeesha, P. S. Subramania Iyer, and Veeraraghavachariar.

Dayong (1893–1929) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe, and taught at the Wuchang Buddhist Institute starting in 1923.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) specialized in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Dineschandra Sircar and served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.
Debamitra Dey is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed her BA Honours in Sanskrit (1997–2000) and her PhD (2003–2008) at Jadavpur University.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University. He founded and served as Director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (circa 1969–1989) and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta, later teaching philosophy at City College, Kolkata, and visiting at the University of Calcutta.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and held the chair in Asian art history at the University of Vienna from 1994 to 2015.
Deborah Sutton is a historian and Indologist who earned her PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University. She serves as Professor in Modern South Asian History at Lancaster University (attested 2026).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching positions at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China, where he was attested as an associate professor of religious studies in 2005.

Deepro Chakraborty is an Indologist who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Alberta. He has taught at St. Stephen's College, Gurudas College, and served as a research assistant at Alberta.
